content:
FEEL Expressions in TaktX

General Concept: FEEL (Friendly Enough Expression Language) is a powerful, human-readable expression language designed for business process modeling. In TaktX, FEEL is used to define conditions, calculations, mappings, and logic within BPMN models, making processes more dynamic and adaptable.

Introduction to FEEL

FEEL is designed to be readable and writable by both business users and developers. It is used to express logic in process conditions, data mappings, and decision tables. FEEL supports a wide range of data types, functions, and operators, making it suitable for complex business logic.

Where Can You Use FEEL in TaktX?

  • Gateway Conditions: Decide which path to take in a process based on data.
  • Input/Output Mappings: Transform and map data into and out of tasks, subprocesses, and events.
  • Event Triggers: Define when an event should be triggered based on process data.
  • Loop and Multi-Instance Configuration: Specify collections and logic for repeating activities.
  • Escalation and Error Handling: Express when to throw or catch errors and escalations.

FEEL Syntax and Data Types

  • Numbers: 42, 3.14
  • Strings: "Hello, world!"
  • Booleans: true, false
  • Lists: [1, 2, 3], ["A", "B", "C"]
  • Contexts (Maps): {name: "Alice", age: 30}
  • Dates and Times: date("2025-11-08"), time("14:30:00")

Operators and Functions

  • Arithmetic: amount + tax, price * quantity
  • Comparison: orderTotal > 1000, status = "APPROVED"
  • Logical: approved and inStock, not delivered
  • List Operations: count(items), sum(prices), all items > 0
  • Conditional: if score > 80 then "Pass" else "Fail"
  • Accessing Data: customer.address.city, order[1]

FEEL Built-in Functions

FEEL provides a rich set of built-in functions to help you work with numbers, strings, lists, contexts, dates, and more. These functions make it easy to perform calculations, manipulate data, and express business logic directly in your BPMN models. Below are the main categories and some practical examples:

Numeric Functions

  • abs(n): Absolute value. abs(-5) → 5
  • max(list): Largest value. max([1, 2, 3]) → 3
  • min(list): Smallest value. min([1, 2, 3]) → 1
  • sum(list): Total. sum([1, 2, 3]) → 6
  • round(n, scale): Rounds to decimal places. round(3.1415, 2) → 3.14

String Functions

  • substring(s, start, length): Extracts part of a string. substring("Hello", 2, 3) → ell
  • string length(s): Length of a string. string length("abc") → 3
  • lower case(s): lower case("ABC") → abc
  • upper case(s): upper case("abc") → ABC
  • contains(s, search): contains("TaktX", "X") → true

List Functions

  • count(list): Number of items. count([1,2,3]) → 3
  • append(list, item): Add item. append([1,2], 3) → [1,2,3]
  • remove(list, item): Remove item. remove([1,2,3], 2) → [1,3]
  • reverse(list): reverse([1,2,3]) → [3,2,1]
  • distinct values(list): distinct values([1,2,2,3]) → [1,2,3]

Context Functions

  • get value(context, key): get value({a:1, b:2}, "b") → 2
  • put(context, key, value): put({a:1}, "b", 2) → {a:1, b:2}
  • keys(context): keys({a:1, b:2}) → ["a", "b"]

Date and Time Functions

  • date(string): date("2025-11-08") → 2025-11-08
  • now(): Current date/time. now()
  • day of week(date): day of week(date("2025-11-08")) → 6 (Saturday)
  • duration(from, to): duration(date("2025-11-08"), date("2025-11-10")) → P2D

Boolean and Miscellaneous Functions

  • not(value): Logical negation. not(true) → false
  • is defined(value): Checks if a value is not null. is defined(customer.email)
  • coalesce(a, b, ...): Returns first non-null. coalesce(null, "A", "B") → A

For a full list and details, see the Camunda FEEL Built-in Functions Guide. In TaktX, these functions can be used anywhere a FEEL expression is allowed, making your BPMN models more expressive and powerful.

Working with Lists and Contexts

FEEL makes it easy to work with collections and structured data:

  • List Creation: [1, 2, 3]
  • List Access: orders[2] (second item)
  • List Functions: count(orders), sum(order.items.price)
  • Context Creation: {name: "Alice", age: 30}
  • Context Access: customer.address.city

Conditional Logic

FEEL supports if-then-else expressions for decision making:

if orderTotal > 1000 then "VIP" else "Standard"

Use this to route processes, set variables, or trigger events based on data.

Null and Missing Values

FEEL handles nulls gracefully. If a variable or property is missing, the result is null. You can check for nulls using is null or is not null:

if customer.email is null then "No email" else customer.email

Dates and Times

  • Date Creation: date("2025-11-08")
  • Time Creation: time("14:30:00")
  • Date Arithmetic: date("2025-11-08") + duration("P1D") (adds one day)

FEEL in Action: Practical Examples

1. Gateway Condition

orderAmount > 1000

This expression routes the process down a specific path if the order amount is greater than 1000.

2. Input Mapping for a Subprocess

inputCollection: orders

Passes the orders list into a multi-instance subprocess.

3. Output Mapping

outputElement: processedOrder

Maps the result of each instance to processedOrder for aggregation.

4. Escalation Trigger

if paymentStatus = "FAILED" then true else false

Triggers an escalation if the payment status is "FAILED".

5. Working with Lists

sum(order.items.price)

Calculates the total price of all items in an order.

Tips for Using FEEL in TaktX

  • Keep expressions simple and readable for maintainability.
  • Use FEEL to centralize business logic in your BPMN models.
  • Test expressions with sample data to ensure correctness.
  • Document complex expressions for future reference.
  • Remember that FEEL expressions are evaluated in the context of the current variable scope.

Further Reading

  • Camunda FEEL Language Guide
  • Variable Handling in TaktX
  • Event Subprocesses
